newsitem.title: USA: Texaco capital spending up 15 pct from 1995. [CORRECTED 19:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Texaco capital spending up 15 pct from 1995. [CORRECTED 19:00 GMT]

text.p: Texaco's capital spending from 1997 through 2001 will total $24.3 billion, chief executive Peter Bijur said Wednesday.
He told analysts that 67 percent of this amount will go to exploration and development while 27 percent is earmarked for refining and marketing.

He said spending for the first nine months of 1996 was $2.52 billion and projected capital spending for the full year would be up 15 percent from last year's $3.1 billion (corrects from $2.7 billion).

Bijur said the company expects its return on capital employed to decline to 11.5 percent next year from 12.4 percent this year, then increase to 13 percent in 1998, 13.4 percent in 1999, 14.4 percent in 2000 and 15.2 percent in 2001.
Later Vice President Patrick J. Lynch pointed out the projected capital spending over the next five years, of $24.3 billion, compares to $15.7 billion spent from 1992 through 1996.
